summary: Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indology scholar who earned his BA and D.Litt. from the University of Mumbai and studied at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He served at Rajaram College, Shivaji University, and the University of Mysore.

Adolf Ellegard Jensen was a religious studies and archaeology scholar who studied under Leo Frobenius. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1923–1939, 1946–1965), Museum der Weltkulturen (1936–1965), and Goethe University Frankfurt (1946–1965).

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin, Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, Kosegarten, Chézy, Silvestre de Sacy, and Freytag, later serving at Breslau University Library and the University of Breslau (1833–1872).

Adolf Holtzmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, and Munich under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. He was Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University from 1852 to 1870.

Adolf Kaegi, an Indology and linguistics scholar, studied at Zurich, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Rudolf von Roth and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He spent his career at the University of Zurich from 1875, becoming full professor of Sanskrit and philology in 1893.

Adolf Kirchhoff worked in linguistics and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh, later holding posts at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he was appointed ordentlicher Professor in 1865.
Adolf Noreen was a Swedish linguist who studied at Uppsala University and under August Leskien in 1879. He held an academic post at Uppsala University from around 1877 to 1919.

Adolph Kießling was a classical scholar who studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker. He held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), the University of Greifswald (~1877–1889), and the University of Göttingen.

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Collège de France, the École Normale Supérieure, the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and as librarian at the Palace of Fontainebleau.

Adriaan Scharpé was an Indologist who completed his doctoral degree at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978) and professor at Ghent University (~1958–1983).
Adrian Kuzminski is a philosopher and Indology scholar. He taught at the University of Hawaiʻi and was a resident scholar in philosophy at Hartwick College in 1997.

Adrian Zenz is a Tibetology and Sinology scholar who earned his PhD at Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He served at the European School of Culture and Theology and joined the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation as a Senior Fellow in 2019.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo and the University of Bonn, and held posts at the University of Warsaw attested between 2008 and 2026.

Agehananda Bharati was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Vienna. He taught at several institutions in India and Japan before serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny is a Tibetologist and archaeologist who studied at the Warsaw Academy of Fine Arts and Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń. She was affiliated with Cornell University (~2008–2010) and held a post at the University of Warsaw in 2015.

Agvan Dorjiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (1880–1888), receiving the Geshe-Lharampa degree. He founded Datsan Gunzechoinei and taught the 13th Dalai Lama and Geshe Wangyal.

Agvan Dorzhiev was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who received the Geshey Lharampa degree at Drepung Monastery's Gomang Dratsang in 1873. He taught the 13th Dalai Lama and Geshe Wangyal, and founded Atsagat Datsan in 1913.

Ahmad Hasan Dani was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington. He held major posts at the University of Dhaka, University of Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam University.

Aiko Okoshi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1970–1975). In 1990, she became a full-time lecturer at Kindai University.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist teacher who studied under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho after graduating from Bedford College. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) before becoming abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in 2010.
